description: Lee Mack's opening series establishes the format: one hundred contestants face increasingly selective logic questions based on language, pictures, numbers and literal wording rather than specialist knowledge.

s01e01.description: Homophones turn pause, paws, mouse and pours into a deceptively simple sound puzzle, while another question asks how many pets Stella owns after accounting for dogs, cats and rabbits. The final challenge hides ONE PERCENT backwards in a broken letter sequence.

s01e02.description: Rhyming children's characters, an impossible London skyline, handed tennis twins and twenty newspaper pages lead into wordplay on SEVENTY-SEVEN and a compressed phrase that resolves to DEEP IN THOUGHT. A later animal splice turns part of GOAT and COW into CAT.

s01e03.description: Words, number patterns and visual relationships steadily tighten before the final puzzle asks contestants to count every triangle hidden inside an overlapping geometric figure, the sort of diagram designed to punish anyone who stops after seeing the obvious shapes.

s01e04.description: A bat-and-ball price trap sits beside questions involving Bring Up the Bodies and a word ladder from HE to HER, HERO and HEROINE. The final asks for a word whose five vowels appear in alphabetical order, producing FACETIOUS.

s01e05.description: TIE hides inside parties, a zookeeper joins an animal-leg count and a one-equals-five reversal tests whether contestants are reading the rule rather than assuming it. The last puzzle asks for the first written number whose letters are in alphabetical order: FORTY.

s01e06.description: Country-name wordplay and positional clues eventually give way to an ordinal sequence: letters are extracted from FIRST, SECOND, THIRD and FOURTH, with the missing next letter coming from FIFTH. The challenge is less arithmetic than noticing where the sequence is looking.

s01e07.description: A late word puzzle presents TROJAN, DISMAY, TRANSEPT, CONCOCT and JUSTIFY and asks for the odd one out. JUSTIFY is the intended answer because the others conceal month endings such as Jan, May, Sept and Oct, though the set is mischievous enough to invite alternate logic.

s01e08.description: TEN is inserted to create POTENTIAL, a rebus resolves to MESSAGE IN A BOTTLE and a counting question punishes anyone who counts what is implied rather than what is actually present. The ladder finishes with another visual-language trap involving a lion.
